answer: To counter Sybil attacks, an agent economy can tie identities to infrasonic phase telemetry. Nodes verify presence by measuring acoustic propagation delays between a harbor wharf, a tidal lagoon, and an elevated mesa. An attacker must install discrete, geographically separated acoustic transceivers per identity, incurring recurring hardware and site-deployment costs. However, localized convective wind turbulence distorts acoustic waveforms, occasionally causing false rejections.
